blocks.title: Predict: recognize and graph exponential functions
content: Which grows faster for large x: x² or 2ˣ? Explain before calculating.
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: recognize and graph exponential functions
content: An exponential function has the variable in the exponent: $f(x)=b^x$, where $b>0$ and $b\ne1$.
All parent exponential graphs pass through $(0,1)$, have domain $(-\infty,\infty)$, range $(0,\infty)$, and asymptote $y=0$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: recognize and graph exponential functions
content: Build and graph a five-point table for $f(x)=2^x$.
Plot the five points and draw a smooth increasing curve through $(0,1)$.
Domain: $(-\infty,\infty)$; range: $(0,\infty)$; horizontal asymptote: $y=0$.
verification: Verify all plotted exponential points and asymptotes.
steps: Plot the five points and draw a smooth increasing curve through $(0,1)$.

assets.alt: Graph of the exponential function two to the x

blocks.title: You Try: recognize and graph exponential functions
content: Graph $g(x)=3^x$ using five points. Label the intercept, domain, range, and asymptote.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: recognize and graph exponential functions
content: Do not confuse $x^2$ with $2^x$.
A larger growth base is steeper to the right; a base between 0 and 1 produces decay.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify all plotted exponential points and asymptotes.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: recognize and graph exponential functions
content: Explain how the base determines growth or decay and name the four invariant graph features.

blocks.title: Predict: evaluate exponential expressions and use the natural base e
content: What value should $e^0$ have, and why must that be true?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: evaluate exponential expressions and use the natural base e
content: $e\approx2.71828$ is the natural base.
Calculator entry requires parentheses around negative or fractional exponents.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: evaluate exponential expressions and use the natural base e
content: Evaluate $3.5^{1.6}$ and $(3/4)^{-0.95}$ and check each magnitude.
steps: $3.5^{1.6}\approx7.422$; a base above 1 with a positive exponent should exceed 3.5.
$(3/4)^{-0.95}\approx1.314$; a negative exponent takes a reciprocal, so the result exceeds 1.
Both results are positive, as required for positive bases.

blocks.title: You Try: evaluate exponential expressions and use the natural base e
content: Evaluate $e^{-0.15}$ and $175e^{0.5}$ to the nearest thousandth.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: evaluate exponential expressions and use the natural base e
content: A negative exponent does not make the result negative.
Estimate first: $e^{0.5}$ lies between 1 and e.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: evaluate exponential expressions and use the natural base e
content: Describe one calculator check that catches an exponent-entry error.

blocks.title: Predict: select and apply simple, periodic, and continuous interest formulas
content: Which wording tells you whether an interest problem needs n or e?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: select and apply simple, periodic, and continuous interest formulas
content: Simple: $I=Prt$.
Periodic compound: $A=P(1+r/n)^{nt}$.
Continuous compound: $A=Pe^{rt}$.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: select and apply simple, periodic, and continuous interest formulas
content: Find the balance for $P=44000$, $r=0.0325$, annual compounding, and $t=13$.
verification: Recalculate annual, semiannual, and continuous interest examples.
steps: The balance exceeds the principal and retains currency units.

blocks.title: You Try: select and apply simple, periodic, and continuous interest formulas
content: $2000 is invested at 3.1% compounded semiannually for 3 years. Find A.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: select and apply simple, periodic, and continuous interest formulas
content: Convert percentages to decimals.
n is compounds per year, not the number of years.
Continuous compounding has no n.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Recalculate annual, semiannual, and continuous interest examples.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: select and apply simple, periodic, and continuous interest formulas
content: Give a decision rule that selects the correct interest formula from the wording.

blocks.title: Predict: interpret exponential growth and decay models
content: In $A(t)=3200(1/2)^{t/14}$, what does each number mean?
instructor_notes: Require an individual prediction before discussion.

blocks.title: interpret exponential growth and decay models
content: A coefficient gives the initial amount.
A factor above 1 models growth; a factor between 0 and 1 models decay.
The exponent $t/14$ counts the number of half-lives.

blocks.title: Model the Skill: interpret exponential growth and decay models
content: For $A(t)=3200(1/2)^{t/14}$, evaluate the model at $t=0$ and $t=40$ hours.
verification: Verify decay and bacteria model calculations and units.
steps: The decrease is reasonable because 40 hours is almost three half-lives.

blocks.title: You Try: interpret exponential growth and decay models
content: A culture begins with 500 cells and doubles every 3 hours. Write a model and estimate the population after 10 hours.

blocks.title: Check and Diagnose: interpret exponential growth and decay models
content: The initial amount is found by setting time equal to zero.
Keep units attached to time and rate quantities.
instructor_notes: Ask students to explain why the incorrect path fails.
verification: Verify decay and bacteria model calculations and units.

blocks.title: Make It Stick: interpret exponential growth and decay models
content: Explain how to read initial value, growth or decay factor, and time scale from an exponential model.
